messages.author: 249e746aeb40b2a0
messages.subject: State-space modeling with multiple observations
parts:
Dear INLA community,


I am hoping to use INLA for a state-space model of population dynamics. After some reading, I understand how to use augmented matrices, estimating separate likelihoods on two columns. However, in my case, I have multiple observations of an animal’s abundance (counts) per site (i.e. multiple plots per site). I would like to use the plot level information to estimate a site level mean:


y_(i,j,k)~rpois(μ_(j,k) ), where plot i is nested in site j for year k     


In my data, I have 941 total plots divided among 99 sites (hence there is an uneven number of plots per site; it ranges from 6 to 24) for 52 years. I have a covariate measured annually at the site level as well as an adjacency matrix for the sites. My goal is to test whether the effect of the covariate on counts varies from year-to-year.


If I ignored the grouping of plots into sites and measured everything at the plot level, my data would look like (and here I am indebted to Ruiz-Cardenas et al. 2010 and Ross et al. 2015):

 

nd <- n.plots*n.years

Y <- matrix(NA, nd*2-n.plots, 2) #second half of data will not contain the final year

Y[1:nd, 1] <- my.data$Count #counts in first column followed by NAs

Y[1:(nd-n.plots) + nd, 2] <- 0 #NAs in second column followed by 0

 

id1  <- (1:nd)[-((1:n.plots)*n.years)] #density dependence will have the last year removed

id2  <- (1:nd)[-c(1,((1:(n.plots-1))*n.years)+1)] #w_t will have the first year removed

ix1  <- c(1:nd, id2)  ## all years for observation model, missing first year for process model

ix1b <- c(rep(NA,nd), id1) ## indices for density dependence

wx1b <- c(rep(1,nd), rep(-1,nd-n.plots)) ## weights for density dependence

iw22 <- c(rep(NA,nd),id2) ## indices for w_t

 

i.plots<-c(rep(NA,nd),as.numeric(factor(my.data$plot))[-((1:n.plots)*n.years)]) #plot level spatial autocorrelation

i.years<-c(rep(NA,nd), as.numeric(factor(my.data$year))[-((1:n.plots)*n.years)])

i.covariate<-c(rep(NA,nd), Covariate$Value[-((1:n.plots)*n.years)]) #plot level measure of covariate

 

dat.try=list(Y=Y, ix1=ix1,ix1b=ix1b,wx1b=wx1b,iw22=iw22,covariate=i.covariate, space=i.plots, time=i.years, ) 

 

formula <- Y ~ f(iw22,model="iid") +   f(ix1, model="iid",initial=-10, fixed=TRUE) + f(ix1b,wx1b, copy="ix1",fixed=FALSE) + f(space, model="bym", graph=adj.plots) + f(time, covariate, model="iid")

 

m.1 <- inla(formula, data = dat.try, family = c("poisson","gaussian"),

               control.family = list(list(link="log"),

                                     list(initial=10, fixed=TRUE)),

               control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE),

               control.compute=list(dic=TRUE,cpo=TRUE))

 

However, I am not clear whether it is possible to implement the model such that the observation and process models have different lengths (941 observations in the observation model and 99 in the process model) and how does the program “know” how to group the plots into the appropriate site.

 

I have seen a similar method applied in Ross et al. 2012 PLoS One where they have an observation model: y_(i,j,t)~NegBinom(μ_(j,t),∅), and a process model: z_(j,t)~log⁡(μ_(j,t) )~β_(0,j)+β_(1,j,t)+ε_(j,t)+n_(j,t) but unfortunately the code they provided doesn’t show the indices for the data matrix.

 

Thank you very much for any help or hints.

Hello,

I am running a similar model as in Ross et al. 2015. Ecological Applications 25: 1606-1617. My main modification is with the observation model, where I am hoping I can use observations (of animal counts) of multiple plots per site to improve the estimate of site-level population size. As well, I am hoping to have a time-varying estimate of the effect of a covariate on population size. The latter part I have successfully implemented in BUGS. Well, only partly successful; the models didn't quite converge and took forever to run, which is why I am switching to INLA.

y_(i,j,k)~rpois(μ_(j,k) ) #observation model where each plot level observation is drawn from a poisson distribution with a site-level mean

z_(j,k) = log((μ_(j,k))) = a + B1*z_(j,k-1) + u_j + B2_k-1*covariate_(j,k-1)  #process model where site-level means are a function of the previous year's population size (density dependence), a spatially autocorrelated random effect for site (u_j), and a covariate sampled at each site; the effect of the covariate can vary over time (year_k)

Thank you!

Have you tried the AR(1) structure with f(z,model="ar1")? And then use
copy (or replicate) so that each time series is its own series?

I've just dug out some old code with this in it (Site and Site2 are sites):
formula=SpeciesTotal~f(Site, model="iid") + f(Site2, Year, model="iid") + Year+
f(i, model="ar1", replicate=Site, fixed=FALSE)
I would have to check the full code to give a workable example, though.

messages.subject: Re: State-space modeling with multiple observations
parts:
Thank you, Bob. I had seen "replicate" before but didn't investigate it further. In fact, the Ross et al. 2012 PLoS One paper uses that notation [i.e., f(space, replicate=time), f(time, replicate=space)] but because they do not show the observation model, I was unsure how to use replicate in a state-space context. 

I tried implementing f(z, model="ar1') on a subset of my data. It runs but I'm not sure it's giving the proper results. The model returns random effects of "i" and "j" (the indices of x_t and x_(t-1)) equal in length to the total data (n.plots*n.sites*n.years) whereas I was expecting the estimates at the site level n.sites*n.years. I imagine I am coding the indices incorrectly.
  
In my test case, I have 2 sites and 12 years. In site 1, I have 10 plots and in site 2, I have 11 plots. Therefore, I am expecting 24 random effects estimates. However, after running the model, I am getting 504 estimates for "i" and "j" (21 plots*12 years*2 transects). The year and spatial autocorrelation random effects seem correct; the former has a length of 22 (n.sites*(n.years-1)) and the latter a length of 48 (n.sites*n.years).
  
I will describe my data and model but I am also attaching R and RData files.

py<-n.plots*n.years #21 plots x 12 years  
sy<-n.sites*n.years #2 sites x 12 years

#Data 
Y <- matrix(NA, py+sy-n.sites, 2) 
Y[1:(n.py, 1] <- data$Count #Counts for every year in every plot, followed by NAs
Y[1:(sy-n.sites) + (py), 2] <- 0 #NAs at the plot level and 0's at the site level
  
So, here my data matrix is "uneven," with the first part consisting of plot level data (n.plots*n.years = 21*12 = 252) and the second part consisting of the site level data (because the 0's of the latent variable are at the site level; n.sites*n.years = 2*12 = 24 - the last year of data at each of the two sites = 22)

#Indices    
id1  <- (1:sy)[-((1:n.sites)*n.years)] #last year removed from each site
id2  <- (1:sy)[-c(1,((1:(n.sites-1))*n.years)+1)] #first year removed from each site
    
i  <- c(1:py, id2) # indices for x_t; 
j  <- c(rep(NA,py), id1)     # indices for x_{t-1}; 
w1 <- c(rep(1,py), rep(-1,(sy-n.sites)))  # weights for j

Here, I wasn't sure if I should have two different "site" index variables. One concatenates: a replication of sites for each of the corresponding plots and years (e.g. site #1 replicated 120 times for each of its 10 plots and 12 years) and a replication of sites for each year (e.g replicated 12 times). The second site index concatenates: a replication of NA for each plot and year followed by the replication for year.
    
i.site.1<-c(as.numeric(factor(data$Site)), rep(as.numeric(factor(unique(data$Site))), each=n.years)[id2])
i.site.2<-c(rep(NA, py), rep(as.numeric(factor(unique(data$Site))), each=n.years)[id2])
i.years<-c(rep(NA,py), rep(as.numeric(factor(unique(data$Year))), times=n.sites)[id2])
i.covariate<-c(rep(NA,py),covariate$Total[-((1:n.sites)*n.years)])
    
dat.try=list(Y=Y, i=i, j=j, w1=w1, cov=i.covariate,
             space.1=i.site.1, space.2=i.site.2, time=i.years)

formula <- Y ~ f(i, model="ar1", replicate=space.1, fixed=FALSE) + f(j, w1, copy="i") + 
  f(space.2, model="bym", graph=adj.s, replicate=time) + f(time, cov, model="iid", replicate=space.2)
    
After running the model, the estimates of "i" and "j" have a length of 504. Can anyone point out my mistake? 

Thank you!!

Hi,
Haakon here. I ran your code and looked at the variables.

str(dat.try, 1)
shows that your linear predictor is of length 274.

but
length(unique(dat.try$i))
= 252
length(unique(dat.try$space.1))
= 2

And so, the latent model ("below the linear predictor"), for i
f(i, model="ar1", replicate=space.1, fixed=FALSE)

has 252*2 = 504 different marginals that you are estimating.
(This f() wants 2 identically distributed replicates of 252 variables)

As I read you, you only wanted 24, from 2 sites in 12 years.
Then, make sure that 
length(unique(dat.try$i)) = 12

Does that help?

Kind regards,
Haakon Bakka

If I understand you correctly, yes, you want to choose the same "i" for all 11 (and later 10) plots in the same transect.

However, how you write it now, you are saying the last year of the first transect (i=12) is connected to the first year of the second transect (i=13). I do not think this is what you want.

If you want to have the SAME effect, not just a shared mean, you can drop the replicate

# Copy?
I do not understand why you have j as a copy of i. This makes me a bit hesitant about my answers. 

# Index across obs likelihoods
In the model you sent me, there was "i" indices across both "observation likelihoods". This is strange to me, do you want the same effect? I would probably use a separate replication index for this other likelihood. Same index (when both in i and the replicator index) means you get the exact same random variable (with same posterior mean estimate and marginal).

Using "copy" and indices "i" across both likelihoods comes from the state-space literature, specifically Ruiz-Cardenes, Krainski, and Rue. 2012. Computational Statistics and Data Analysis 56:1808-1828.

Stealing directly from their code available on r-inla.org

set.seed(123456)

W = 0.5
V = 1.0
n = 100
x0 = 0.00
w  = rnorm(n,0,sqrt(W))
v  = rnorm(n,0,sqrt(V))
x  = y = rep(0,n)
x[1] = x0   + w[1]
y[1] = x[1] + v[1]
for (t in 2:n){
  x[t] = x[t-1] + w[t]
  y[t] = x[t]   + v[t]
}

m = n-1

# building the augmented model
# ----------------------------
Y <- matrix(NA, n+m, 2)
Y[1:n,     1] <- y              # actual observations
Y[1:m + n, 2] <- 0              # faked observations


# indices for the INLA library
# ----------------------------
i  <- c(1:n, 2:n)              # indices for x_t
j  <- c(rep(NA,n), 2:n -1)     # indices for x_{t-1}
w1 <- c(rep(NA,n), rep(-1,m))  # weights for j
l  <- c(rep(NA,n), 1:m)        # indices for w_t


# formulating the model
# ---------------------
formula <- Y ~ f(i, model="iid", initial=-10, fixed=T) +
f(j, w1, copy="i") +
f(l, model ="iid") -1

Dear INLA community,


I am hoping to use INLA for a state-space model of population dynamics. After some reading, I understand how to use augmented matrices, estimating separate likelihoods on two columns. However, in my case, I have multiple observations of an animal’s abundance (counts) per site (i.e. multiple plots per site). I would like to use the plot level information to estimate a site level mean:


y_(i,j,k)~rpois(μ_(j,k) ), where plot i is nested in site j for year k     


In my data, I have 941 total plots divided among 99 sites (hence there is an uneven number of plots per site; it ranges from 6 to 24) for 52 years. I have a covariate measured annually at the site level as well as an adjacency matrix for the sites. My goal is to test whether the effect of the covariate on counts varies from year-to-year.


If I ignored the grouping of plots into sites and measured everything at the plot level, my data would look like (and here I am indebted to Ruiz-Cardenas et al. 2010 and Ross et al. 2015):

 

nd <- n.plots*n.years

Y <- matrix(NA, nd*2-n.plots, 2) #second half of data will not contain the final year

Y[1:nd, 1] <- my.data$Count #counts in first column followed by NAs

Y[1:(nd-n.plots) + nd, 2] <- 0 #NAs in second column followed by 0

 

id1  <- (1:nd)[-((1:n.plots)*n.years)] #density dependence will have the last year removed

id2  <- (1:nd)[-c(1,((1:(n.plots-1))*n.years)+1)] #w_t will have the first year removed

ix1  <- c(1:nd, id2)  ## all years for observation model, missing first year for process model

ix1b <- c(rep(NA,nd), id1) ## indices for density dependence

wx1b <- c(rep(1,nd), rep(-1,nd-n.plots)) ## weights for density dependence

iw22 <- c(rep(NA,nd),id2) ## indices for w_t

 

i.plots<-c(rep(NA,nd),as.numeric(factor(my.data$plot))[-((1:n.plots)*n.years)]) #plot level spatial autocorrelation

i.years<-c(rep(NA,nd), as.numeric(factor(my.data$year))[-((1:n.plots)*n.years)])

i.covariate<-c(rep(NA,nd), Covariate$Value[-((1:n.plots)*n.years)]) #plot level measure of covariate

 

dat.try=list(Y=Y, ix1=ix1,ix1b=ix1b,wx1b=wx1b,iw22=iw22,covariate=i.covariate, space=i.plots, time=i.years, ) 

 

formula <- Y ~ f(iw22,model="iid") +   f(ix1, model="iid",initial=-10, fixed=TRUE) + f(ix1b,wx1b, copy="ix1",fixed=FALSE) + f(space, model="bym", graph=adj.plots) + f(time, covariate, model="iid")

 

m.1 <- inla(formula, data = dat.try, family = c("poisson","gaussian"),

               control.family = list(list(link="log"),

                                     list(initial=10, fixed=TRUE)),

               control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE),

               control.compute=list(dic=TRUE,cpo=TRUE))

 

However, I am not clear whether it is possible to implement the model such that the observation and process models have different lengths (941 observations in the observation model and 99 in the process model) and how does the program “know” how to group the plots into the appropriate site.

 

I have seen a similar method applied in Ross et al. 2012 PLoS One where they have an observation model: y_(i,j,t)~NegBinom(μ_(j,t),∅), and a process model: z_(j,t)~log⁡(μ_(j,t) )~β_(0,j)+β_(1,j,t)+ε_(j,t)+n_(j,t) but unfortunately the code they provided doesn’t show the indices for the data matrix.

 

Thank you very much for any help or hints.

Hi,


Thank you for the reply. I would love to hear more about why or if I do not need the fake zeroes. I’ll try the best I can to describe my aims mathematically, though, I have very little experience and training doing so (which, is a part of the problem...). So apologies if the notation just makes things more confusing.


y_(i,j,t)~rpois(μ_(j,t) ) #observation model

z_(j,t)~log(μ_(j,t) )~β_0(j)+β_1(j)*z_(j,t-1)+ε_(j,t)+n_(j,t) #process model

ε_(j,t) ~ N(π_(j,t), σ2) #second level of the hierarchical model

π_(j,t) ~ α_1 + α_2(t) *covariate_(j,t) + ω_(j, t) #second level process model


n_(j,t) has a spatially autocorrelated error structure

 

The key points are:

- Plot level observations (y_(i,j,t)) from the same site are drawn from a poisson distribution with the same mean

- The site level mean (and, thus, the observations) are related to the previous year’s mean (i.e. density dependence)

- The estimate I’m most interested in solving is α_2, which dictates the effect of the covariate on population size every year. In essence, I want to know year-to-year variation in the magnitude and direction of the effect of the covariate. And the effect is to be measured after controlling for the effects of density dependence and spatial autocorrelation.
